events.title: Nvidia signs $27 billion structured deal with Poolside
events.summary: On 2026-08-25, Nvidia reportedly signed a $27 billion technology-license and investment arrangement with Poolside.ai. Poolside’s 109 engineers are joining Nvidia’s Nemotron team while Poolside remains nominally independent. The structure is being scrutinized as a possible way to avoid Hart-Scott-Rodino merger review, though no enforcement action has been taken.

events.title: Anthropic signs $35 billion cloud infrastructure agreement with Lambda
events.summary: On 2026-09-01, Anthropic and Lambda were reported to have reached an estimated $35 billion cloud agreement in the United States. The arrangement gives Anthropic multi-year access to high-performance infrastructure, with Nvidia providing investment and technology support. The article links the deal to the construction of a supercomputing center in Texas and intensifying competition for AI capacity.

events.title: Inspur subsidiary allegedly bypassed US blacklist for AI chip exports
events.summary: On 2026-09-07, reporting disclosed that Inspur Group renamed its California subsidiary Aivres after Inspur was blacklisted by U.S. authorities. According to the report, the subsidiary continued operating with the same workforce and allegedly routed more than $5.6 billion in advanced AI technology, including Nvidia Blackwell-based servers, through Southeast Asia to China. The development indicates

events.title: Nvidia backs $105 billion Ohio data center project
events.summary: On 2026-08-18, Nvidia confirmed financial backing of SoftBank's SB Energy data-center project at the Portsmouth Site in Pike County, Ohio. The project is initially planned for 4.25GW and is fully leased to OpenAI, with potential expansion to 10GW. Nvidia's support is a financing backstop rather than evidence that the facility is operational.

events.title: Qualcomm and AWS sign multigenerational AI silicon deal
events.summary: On 2026-09-08, Qualcomm and Amazon Web Services signed a multigenerational agreement to co-develop custom AI inference chips and optical connectivity hardware. The arrangement includes a warrant for up to 25 million Qualcomm shares, vesting based on as much as $60 billion in AWS spending through 2036. Qualcomm said revenue will begin in its fiscal first quarter of 2027, with chips already in produ

events.title: Nvidia invests $3.5 billion in MediaTek convertible bonds
events.summary: On 2026-09-10, Nvidia reportedly agreed to purchase $3.5 billion of convertible bonds issued by MediaTek. In connection with the investment, MediaTek will adopt Nvidia’s NVLink Fusion technology so customers can connect custom AI accelerators to Nvidia infrastructure. The deal strengthens Nvidia’s AI platform position while giving MediaTek capital and access to Nvidia’s ecosystem.

events.title: Amkor expands Arizona advanced packaging campus to $12 billion
events.summary: On 2026-09-09, Amkor Technology announced Phase 2 of its advanced semiconductor packaging and test campus in Tempe, Arizona. The expansion adds 60,000 square meters of cleanroom space and lifts planned investment to approximately $12 billion. NVIDIA is providing a prepayment under a multiyear strategic partnership supporting the added U.S. capacity.

events.title: SpaceX closes $1.11 billion monthly AI hosting deal
events.summary: On 2026-09-10, SpaceX disclosed that it had closed another AI data-center hosting agreement worth about $1.11 billion per month beginning December 1. The customer was not identified, and the deal adds to SpaceX agreements with Google and Anthropic amid tight AI-compute capacity.

events.title: Nvidia agrees to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9 billion
events.summary: On 2026-09-07, Nvidia reportedly signed a definitive agreement to acquire Hugging Face for approximately $12.9 billion. The transaction includes about $11.9 billion for shareholders and up to $1 billion in employee equity incentives. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approval and customary conditions.

events.title: Anthropic signs $45 billion compute deal with Nscale
events.summary: On 2026-09-01, Anthropic reportedly signed a roughly $45 billion, six-year agreement with Nscale for about 460 megawatts at the Monarch campus in West Virginia. The site is expected to run NVIDIA Vera Rubin chips, but operations are not scheduled to begin until late 2027. The deal is reported ahead of prospective public filings by both companies.

events.title: Nvidia announces $12.9 billion acquisition of Hugging Face
events.summary: On 2026-09-03, Nvidia announced it would buy Hugging Face for more than $12.9 billion. Nvidia said the open AI platform would remain open and independent of Nvidia compute requirements, while the acquisition would expand infrastructure, engineering and deployment capabilities for its 18-million-strong userbase.

events.title: Marvell grants Google warrant for potential $12.2 billion stake
events.summary: On 2026-08-19, Marvell Technology granted Google a warrant to purchase up to 58.97 million Marvell shares at $206.58 each. The potential stake is valued at about $12.18 billion and is tied to Google’s purchasing targets through fiscal 2033. The companies will work together on custom chips supporting Google’s TPU ecosystem.

events.title: Nvidia agrees to acquire AI platform Hugging Face for $12.9 billion
events.summary: On 2026-08-31, Nvidia reportedly agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9 billion. The transaction would give Nvidia control of Hugging Face’s open-model distribution and collaboration platform, though neither company had publicly detailed the terms and completion was not reported.

events.title: Nvidia agrees to buy Hugging Face for $12.93 billion
events.summary: On 2026-09-05, Nvidia agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12.93 billion in Santa Clara, California. The deal includes approximately $11.9 billion for Hugging Face investors and up to $1 billion in equity-based employee retention awards. The acquisition would expand Nvidia's access to developers using open AI models and tools, while some analysts raised concerns about possible competitive effects o

events.title: China eases restrictions on Nvidia H200 AI chips
events.summary: On 2026-08-19, Chinese authorities reportedly permitted small shipments of Nvidia H200 processors to leading domestic technology firms including ByteDance and Tencent. The move relaxes earlier restrictions on advanced US AI hardware amid competition with US rivals, though limited mainland infrastructure constrains deployment.

events.title: Nvidia agrees $12.9 billion deal for open-source AI ecosystem
events.summary: On 2026-08-28, Nvidia reportedly agreed to a $12.9 billion deal to take control of an open-source artificial-intelligence ecosystem. The title does not identify the target company or provide details on transaction structure, regulatory status, or completion.

events.title: Firmus signs OpenAI deal for Malaysian AI data centers
events.summary: On 2026-09-10, Australian Firmus reportedly signed a multi-year agreement to provide OpenAI capacity in Malaysia. OpenAI will serve as the anchor customer for two AI data centers, while Firmus said its contracted capacity would exceed 900 MW. The facilities are intended to support growing regional and global demand for OpenAI products.

events.title: Razorpay builds AI payments model from four billion transactions
events.summary: On 2026-08-18, Razorpay reportedly built an AI payments foundation model trained on four billion transactions. The company says it aims to improve payment success rates, fraud detection, and checkout personalization as India's digital payments ecosystem grows. Razorpay co-founder and CEO Harshil Mathur is identified in the article's coverage.

events.title: Samsung and ASML expand High-NA EUV partnership
events.summary: On 2026-09-08, Samsung and ASML expanded cooperation on High-NA EUV lithography and advanced photomask solutions. Samsung will help develop a next-generation 12-inch photomask platform intended to support future advanced semiconductor and DRAM production. The reported development has strategic significance for semiconductor scaling and AI-related memory supply chains, but no immediate production m

events.title: Nvidia plans major AI compute capacity expansion in Australia
events.summary: On 2026-09-10, Nvidia announced partnerships with Firmus, CDC, NEXTDC and AirTrunk to target up to 2 GW of AI-related data-centre capacity in Australia by 2027. The planned buildout would more than double the country's reported current computing capacity of 1.6 GW and use Nvidia's DSX platform. The article also notes environmental concerns about data-centre energy and water consumption.

events.title: AMD wins $450 million contract for Europe’s LUMI-AI supercomputer
events.summary: On 2026-09-01, EuroHPC JU and the LUMI AI Factory consortium awarded AMD a contract worth approximately $450 million for Europe's LUMI-AI supercomputer. The system will use AMD Instinct MI430X GPUs and EPYC CPUs in Bull's platform, with Nokia networking and IBM storage. The project is intended to expand Europe's sovereign AI capacity.

events.title: Nvidia invests $3.5 billion in MediaTek for AI development
events.summary: On 2026-09-01, Nvidia reportedly invested $3.5 billion in Taiwan-based MediaTek for artificial intelligence development. The title-only report identifies a significant strategic capital allocation but provides no further details on the investment structure or implementation.

events.title: Firmus signs Malaysia data centre capacity deal with OpenAI
events.summary: On 2026-09-08, Australian AI infrastructure firm Firmus signed a multi-year agreement with OpenAI to supply computing capacity from two Malaysian data centres. OpenAI will serve as an anchor customer as Firmus’ contracted capacity rises above 900 MW; financial terms were not reported. The deal comes amid strong AI infrastructure demand and ahead of Firmus’ reportedly anticipated IPO.

events.title: Nscale seeks $3.5 billion ahead of possible IPO
events.summary: On 2026-09-04, British AI infrastructure company Nscale was reportedly seeking $3.5 billion in pre-IPO financing. The package reportedly includes $1.5 billion in convertible notes from investors and a further $2 billion from Nvidia. The financing discussions precede a possible IPO later in September but had not been completed according to the report.

events.title: Lambda raises $1B private debt for Nvidia GPU deal
events.summary: On 2026-08-28, Lambda reportedly raised about $1B in private short-dated debt arranged by JPMorgan. The financing will fund Nvidia GPU purchases that Microsoft will lease, although the terms were not independently verified by The Next Web.

events.title: Cassava and Vodafone announce Egypt data-centre venture
events.summary: On 2026-09-11, Cassava and Vodafone announced plans for a potential $1 billion Egypt data-centre venture targeting up to 200MW of capacity. The partners also announced a separate sovereign-AI infrastructure partnership intended to provide local Nvidia computing services. The article says the investment is not yet spent or irrevocably committed, and the facility location and opening date remain und

events.title: NVIDIA releases PAIR software for personal AI computing clusters
events.summary: On 2026-09-02, NVIDIA reportedly released PAIR as a free, open-source beta. The software discovers compatible PCs and Macs on a local network and distributes AI-agent inference workloads across their idle computing resources. The release represents a commercial technology milestone, although the articles provide no evidence of immediate large-scale market adoption.

events.title: LG and Nvidia expand partnership in humanoid robots and AI factories
events.summary: On 2026-08-14, LG Corp and Nvidia reportedly signed an MOU expanding their strategic partnership in humanoid robotics, AI factories and next-generation mobility. LG plans an Nvidia-powered AI factory reference site in South Korea in the first half of 2027, with expansion to 80 megawatts targeted for the first half of 2028.

events.title: Apple and tech giants face AI voice data lawsuits
events.summary: On 2026-08-21, journalists, podcasters and audiobook narrators reportedly filed nine lawsuits in Chicago against Apple and other technology companies. The plaintiffs allege that recordings were harvested for AI training, while defendants argue the alleged use has not been demonstrated and that the relevant biometric privacy law may not apply.

events.title: Naval Postgraduate School brings military AI supercomputer online
events.summary: On 2026-09-06, the Naval Postgraduate School in Monterey, California, brought the first Nvidia DGX GB300 supercomputer deployed within the U.S. military online. Students, faculty and approved research partners will use it for defense applications including ocean modeling, cybersecurity, autonomous maritime systems and mission planning. The installation is a national military AI-compute infrastruct

events.title: iPronics raises $125 million to expand AI optical switching
events.summary: On 2026-09-10, iPronics reportedly raised $125 million in Series B funding in a round co-led by Maverick Silicon and Light Street Capital, with participation from NVIDIA. The company plans to use the financing to expand operations and commercial deployment of its Optical Networking Engine for AI data centres.

events.title: Etched raises $700 million in new AI chip funding
events.summary: On 2026-08-19, Etched reportedly raised $700 million in a funding round led by Jane Street, with participation from several venture and investment firms. The financing reportedly lifted the AI inference-chip startup's valuation to $21 billion. Etched develops integrated inference chips, racks, software and manufacturing methods.

events.title: Samsung SDS announces 2027 robot orchestration platform
events.summary: On 2026-09-08, Samsung SDS announced at its REAL Summit 2026 event in Seoul that it will launch a robot orchestration platform in 2027. The platform is intended to integrate production equipment and robots for manufacturing customers as the company expands into physical AI and robotics transformation.

events.title: Zeekr produces 200,000th 7X electric SUV globally
events.summary: On 2026-09-08, Zeekr produced its 200,000th 7X electric SUV globally, nearly two years after mass production began. The company is also preparing a 2027 model-year update with an 85 kWh battery for the fourth quarter of 2026. The milestone reflects production rather than completed customer deliveries.

events.title: Nvidia discloses SpaceX as its second-largest holding
events.summary: On 2026-08-15, Nvidia reportedly disclosed that SpaceX is its second-largest holding. The title does not provide the investment amount, acquisition date, or transaction terms, so this is coded as a current capital-allocation disclosure with limited evidence.

events.title: Nepal glacial collapse unleashes devastating Himalayan flood
events.summary: On 2026-08-26, a massive glacial collapse occurred in Nepal’s high Himalayas at about 8:37 AM. According to the reports, a landslide-related glacial lake breach released water, sediment and boulders downstream, causing widespread devastation. Nepal’s disaster authority reportedly sent warning alerts 38 minutes later, with some areas receiving them about an hour after the collapse.

events.title: Nscale seeks $3.5 billion in pre-IPO financing
events.summary: On 2026-09-06, Nscale was reportedly in talks to raise $3.5 billion ahead of a possible IPO later this month. The proposed package includes $1.5 billion in convertible notes and an additional $2 billion from Nvidia. The financing remains under discussion rather than completed.

events.title: Anthropic abandons proposed $6 billion Decart acquisition
events.summary: On 2026-09-08, Anthropic decided not to proceed with its potential acquisition of Israeli AI infrastructure startup Decart after due diligence. The proposed transaction was valued at up to $6 billion, but the companies had not reached a definitive agreement and may pursue other collaboration.

events.title: Groq raises $350 million for AI cloud expansion
events.summary: On 2026-08-17, Groq Inc. announced a $350 million Series A funding round led by returning backer Disruptive. Nvidia is expected to join later, although its investment amount was not specified. Groq said the funds will support expansion of its AI cloud platform.

events.title: TSMC and ASML advance High-NA EUV mask development
events.summary: On 2026-09-08, TSMC and ASML reportedly advanced cooperation on 12-inch High-NA EUV masks in Taiwan. The companies are considering introducing the masks into mass production by 2030, but the title does not report current production or deployment. This represents a developmental milestone in advanced semiconductor manufacturing technology.

events.title: NVIDIA announces DLSS 5 integration for NBA 2K27
events.summary: On 2026-09-01, NVIDIA reportedly announced DLSS 5 integration in NBA 2K27. The title-only report claims the technology will deliver near-realistic graphics, but provides no further details on availability, commercial terms, or scale.

events.title: Nvidia pauses revenue-sharing deals with AI cloud companies
events.summary: On 2026-08-28, Nvidia reportedly paused some revenue-sharing deals with AI cloud companies. The article presents the move as a response to antitrust and control concerns surrounding circular financing arrangements, but provides no deal values or details on affected counterparties.

events.title: Enflame triples in value on Shanghai debut
events.summary: On 2026-09-11, Chinese chipmaker Enflame debuted in Shanghai and reportedly tripled in value at the opening. The title-only report does not provide the offering size, proceeds, or further listing terms.

events.title: Zeekr 7X global orders surpass 200,000 amid overseas expansion
events.summary: On 2026-08-24, Zeekr announced that global orders for its 7X luxury electric SUV had exceeded 200,000 units. The model had reached more than 50 countries and regions, with Mexico's Joaquín Ezcurra placing the 200,000th order. Zeekr said the model ranked first among luxury electric C-SUVs in Mexico from January through July 2026.

events.title: Groq raises $350 million to expand AI inference cloud
events.summary: On 2026-08-19, Groq reportedly raised $350 million in a Series A led by Disruptive, with Nvidia expected to participate. The financing valued Groq at $3.5 billion and followed a $650 million round in June. Groq plans to expand its inference cloud, including 13 data centers and more than 200 megawatts of capacity by 2027.

events.title: Infobip unveils AI-first routers and rapid-deployment agents
events.summary: On 2026-08-20, Infobip reportedly unveiled AI-first smart routers and agent technology from its operations in Vodnjan, Croatia. Its internal platform allows engineers to build and publish production AI agents in approximately two minutes using reusable components, while the company also uses local Nvidia hardware and external model APIs. The article frames this as a commercial technology developme

events.title: OpenAI unveils Astra as Nvidia CEO declares AGI has arrived
events.summary: On 2026-09-03, OpenAI unveiled Astra, which it described as its most intelligent and aligned model. OpenAI President Greg Brockman and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang characterized the release as marking the arrival of the AGI era, but the article provides no independent benchmark or confirmation of general intelligence. The model was trained on Nvidia chips and began rolling out to customers.

events.title: Starcloud raises $250 million for orbital AI data centers
events.summary: On 2026-08-21, Starcloud announced a $250 million extension to its Series A financing, following an original $170 million round. The funding values the AI satellite startup at an estimated $2.3 billion and supports production lines at its 10,000-square-meter Woodinville, Washington facility. The report says Starcloud is developing satellites capable of running AI inference in orbit.

events.title: Gravis Robotics raises $200 million for autonomous equipment technology
events.summary: On 2026-08-18, Gravis Robotics reportedly raised $200 million from investors including SoftBank Group in Zurich. The financing will support the company’s AI-powered autonomous construction equipment technology, which is designed for small and midsized contractors. SoftBank described physical AI as central to its investment strategy.

events.title: Wistron plans $1.5 billion share issuance
events.summary: On 2026-09-08, Wistron reportedly announced plans to issue $1.5 billion in shares. The Taiwanese electronics manufacturer is identified as an Nvidia supplier, but the title provides no further details on the use of proceeds or transaction terms.

events.title: Huawei bids to build AI data centres for Egypt
events.summary: On 2026-08-26, Huawei Technologies bid to build AI data centres for the Egyptian government in Cairo. The proposal includes 2,008 Ascend chips and a 12-month construction schedule. The US State Department is reportedly seeking a rival consortium involving Nvidia, AMD and Microsoft.

events.title: Nvidia joins iPronics in $107 million financing round
events.summary: On 2026-09-07, Nvidia participated in iPronics' $107 million financing round in Valencia, Spain. The round was co-led by Maverick Silicon and Light Street Capital and will fund hiring, commercial deployment of optical switches, and operational expansion. The investment is reportedly Nvidia's first participation in a Spanish company.

events.title: Stratos Lab deploys 400 Nvidia GPUs for South African AI cloud
events.summary: On 2026-08-26, Stratos Lab, Ecoblox and Digital Parks Africa announced deployment of more than 400 Nvidia GPUs in South Africa. The platform is expected to deliver 7.2 exaflops for AI and high-performance computing workloads, expanding local access to advanced compute capacity. The strategic significance is regional AI infrastructure development, though the project is privately led rather than gov

events.title: Dominican government launches AI training program for one million
events.summary: On 2026-09-10, President Luis Abinader presented RD Inteligente in Santo Domingo. The Dominican government will provide free artificial-intelligence training to one million Dominican citizens to improve workplace capabilities, productivity, and employment opportunities.

events.title: Supermicro fires employees after China AI chip smuggling probe
events.summary: On 2026-08-21, Supermicro reportedly fired several employees following an investigation into transactions linked to an alleged $2.5 billion China AI chip diversion scheme. The company said current senior management had no knowledge of the alleged scheme, while warning that previously issued financial statements might be unreliable because of potential export-control diversions.

events.title: Keelung prosecutors indict Nvidia and Supermicro employees
events.summary: On 2026-08-26, Keelung prosecutors in Taiwan indicted nine people over allegedly exporting advanced AI servers to China in violation of U.S. restrictions. The defendants reportedly included a senior Nvidia Taiwan manager and two Supermicro employees, with 74 servers delivered through transit routes including Japan, Hong Kong, and Indonesia.

events.title: United States leverages NVIDIA chip access in Armenia peace talks
events.summary: On 2026-09-07, U.S. negotiators reportedly promised to expand Armenia’s authorized access to NVIDIA AI chips as leverage in negotiations with Azerbaijan. The reported technology-access offer was linked to efforts to reach a preliminary Armenia-Azerbaijan peace agreement. The account was based on Wall Street Journal sources close to the negotiations.

events.title: Starcloud raises $250 million for orbital computing expansion
events.summary: On 2026-08-24, Starcloud announced a $250 million Series A extension at a $2.3 billion post-money valuation. Cisco joined as a new investor, while the proceeds will support manufacturing capacity, engineering with NVIDIA, and future launch allocation in Washington.

events.title: United States urges G20 to avoid new AI regulations
events.summary: On 2026-09-01, the United States urged G20 member countries at a meeting in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, to avoid creating new institutions or rules for governing artificial intelligence. US technology adviser Michael Kratsios also advocated adoption of the Carolina Principles, which reserve new regulation for novel considerations. events.title: Whale Rock cuts most of its Nvidia stake in Q2
events.summary: On 2026-08-23, Whale Rock Capital Management's latest 13F filing showed it reduced its Nvidia holding by about 64%, from approximately 1.04 million shares to 377,204 shares. The filing also showed an increase in Advanced Micro Devices holdings, indicating a portfolio reallocation rather than a complete exit from AI semiconductors.

events.title: TSMC plans major Arizona expansion for advanced chip production
events.summary: On 2026-09-06, TSMC highlighted a major planned investment in Phoenix, Arizona, to expand semiconductor manufacturing. The company planned six Arizona plants, with four additional facilities for chips at 2 nanometers or smaller. US officials said the investment would strengthen the semiconductor supply chain and create technology jobs.

events.title: TSMC enters record expansion to boost Taiwan chip capacity
events.summary: On 2026-09-08, TSMC reportedly entered a record expansion of its Taiwan chip-production capacity in response to the AI boom. The title links the company’s expansion to a broader global semiconductor supply-chain shift, but provides no specific investment amount, facility, or added output figure.

events.title: Samsung Electronics books Taylor fab capacity before pilot launch
events.summary: On 2026-09-08, Samsung Electronics reported that its Taylor, Texas, foundry is expected to begin pilot operation later this month. The planned 2-nanometer output, initially about 50,000 wafers per month, is reportedly already fully booked by customers including Tesla and Broadcom. The update also describes preparations for a second fab at the site.

events.title: TSMC announces Kaohsiung move to expand advanced packaging supply chain
events.summary: On 2026-09-01, TSMC announced that it would move into Baiqyuan Park in Kaohsiung, Taiwan. The initiative is intended to expand the advanced packaging equipment supply chain, although the title provides no investment amount or construction timeline.

The financing reportedly lifted the AI inference-chip startup's valuation to $21 billion. Etched develops integrated inference chips, racks, software and manufacturing methods.

events.title: Lai pledges global chip cooperation amid rising AI demand
events.summary: On 2026-09-01, Taiwan President Lai Ching-te said in Taipei that Taiwan would work with countries worldwide on semiconductors. He said the cooperation would diversify production and build a more resilient supply chain amid AI demand, natural disasters, pandemics, and geopolitical shifts.

events.title: Nvidia discloses SpaceX as its second-largest holding
events.summary: On 2026-08-15, Nvidia reportedly disclosed that SpaceX is its second-largest holding. The title does not provide the investment amount, acquisition date, or transaction terms, so this is coded as a current capital-allocation disclosure with limited evidence.

events.summary: On 2026-09-08, TSMC and ASML reportedly advanced cooperation on 12-inch High-NA EUV masks in Taiwan. The companies are considering introducing the masks into mass production by 2030, but the title does not report current production or deployment. This represents a developmental milestone in advanced semiconductor manufacturing technology.

events.title: SoftBank adds Capital One stake and sells most TSMC holdings
events.summary: On 2026-08-14, SoftBank Group Corp. disclosed that it acquired 276,811 Capital One shares valued at $55.5 million. It also reported selling 1.4 million Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing shares, representing 71.5% of its holding, for $269.8 million during the second quarter. The transactions were disclosed through a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission filing.

events.title: Xiaomi unveils prototype mini-PC for local AI processing
events.summary: On 2026-08-24, Xiaomi unveiled the AI Cube prototype at its XRING chip technology conference in China. The mini-PC combines three proprietary Xring chips for local execution of large AI models without relying on external cloud infrastructure. The report does not establish a benchmark record or operational deployment, so this is coded as a low-magnitude AI capability milestone.

events.title: LG Energy Solution starts production at Lansing battery plant
events.summary: On 2026-08-18, LG Energy Solution began production at its new 226-acre battery facility in Lansing, Michigan. The plant makes LFP cells for energy-storage systems and batteries for electric vehicles, with planned annual capacity exceeding 35 GWh at full scale. LG Energy Solution Vertech will integrate the cells into utility, grid-scale, and commercial energy-storage systems.

events.title: Samsung Electronics books Taylor fab capacity before pilot launch
events.summary: On 2026-09-08, Samsung Electronics reported that its Taylor, Texas, foundry is expected to begin pilot operation later this month. The planned 2-nanometer output, initially about 50,000 wafers per month, is reportedly already fully booked by customers including Tesla and Broadcom. The update also describes preparations for a second fab at the site.

events.title: Tesla proposes $10 billion solar factory near Houston
events.summary: On 2026-08-19, Tesla was reported to be considering a $10.1 billion solar-cell manufacturing facility on a 3,050-acre site in Richmond, Texas. Documents submitted by Kroll to the Texas Comptroller say construction could finish in 2028 and operations begin in 2029, subject to a tax-incentive agreement. The project is projected to create nearly 9,712 full-time jobs and more than 1,100 construction j

events.title: China orders Tesla and automakers to recall over four million cars
events.summary: On 2026-08-21, China's State Administration for Market Regulation announced recalls affecting more than four million vehicles, including nearly three million Teslas. Xiaomi, XPeng and Geely were also ordered to recall more than 750,000 vehicles combined. The action addresses hidden door handles ahead of China's 2027 requirement for mechanical releases and warning labels.

events.title: Elon Musk launches steering-wheel-free Cybercab taxi service in Austin
events.summary: On 2026-09-03, Tesla launched an invitation-based Cybercab autonomous taxi service in Austin, Texas, with dozens of vehicles lacking steering wheels and brake pedals. Elon Musk promoted the rollout as Tesla seeks to expand autonomous taxi operations and compete with Waymo and Zoox. The launch was followed shortly by a reported National Highway Traffic Safety Administration investigation, but this

events.title: Tesla plans $10B solar cell manufacturing plant in Texas
events.summary: On 2026-08-24, Tesla was reported to be considering a solar-cell manufacturing site in Fort Bend County, Texas, under Project Crystal Sun. The proposed facility could cost about $10 billion, create more than 9,712 jobs, and substantially expand Tesla’s current solar capacity, but the company has not selected a final site or committed to construction. Tesla is seeking state property-tax incentives

events.title: Tesla recalls cars in China over dangerous door handles
events.summary: On 2026-09-06, Tesla and eight other automakers reportedly began or continued a recall campaign covering 4.6 million vehicles in China. The defect involves recessed door handles that may become difficult to open after a crash; remedies include software updates and warning stickers.

events.title: Musk launches driverless taxi service
events.summary: On 2026-09-03, Tesla launched paid Cybercab rides in Austin, Texas, using vehicles without steering wheels, pedals, or mirrors. The rollout involved dozens of vehicles and preceded planned expansion to other cities; NHTSA subsequently opened an audit of about 1,000 Cybercabs over compliance with federal safety rules.

events.title: Tesla unveils Cybercab robotaxi without steering controls
events.summary: On 2026-09-10, Tesla unveiled its two-seat Cybercab robotaxi in Austin, Texas. The electric vehicle is designed without a steering wheel or pedals and relies on Tesla's autonomous-driving system; Tesla had registered 45 vehicles with Texas regulators before the event. The company plans to expand robotaxi deployment in the United States, according to the article.

events.title: Tesla unveils Cybercab robotaxi in Tokyo, Japan
events.summary: On 2026-09-11, Tesla reportedly unveiled its fully autonomous two-seat Cybercab to the public in Tokyo’s Aoyama district. The vehicle has no steering wheel, accelerator, or brake pedals and uses eight cameras; Tesla has begun production but does not currently plan to sell it in Japan.

events.title: Uber announces 3,300 layoffs and ends full remote work
events.summary: On 2026-09-06, Uber reportedly announced plans to cut about 3,300 employees, or roughly 10% of its workforce. The company is also reducing management layers and requiring most remote workers to spend at least three days per week in offices. Uber said the restructuring is intended to redirect resources toward autonomous vehicles, delivery, and other growth opportunities.

events.title: Tesla unveils Cybercab robotaxi in Austin, Texas
events.summary: On 2026-09-03, Tesla sent dozens of Cybercabs without steering wheels or brake pedals onto public streets in Austin, Texas. The vehicles rely completely on Tesla's autonomous driving system, marking a live deployment of a novel autonomous transport service. The rollout was limited and invitation-only, with expansion to other cities being prepared.

events.title: Tesla, Uber and Waymo get approval to operate thousands of robotaxis in Nevada
events.summary: On 2026-08-20, the Nevada Transportation Authority unanimously approved permits for Tesla, Waymo, and Uber to operate commercial robotaxi services in Clark County. The permits allow deployment of up to 8,000 autonomous vehicles over the next 12 months, potentially making Las Vegas a major robotaxi market. Uber's operations will involve partnerships with Motional and Zoox.

events.title: Tesla launches Model Y Performance in China
events.summary: On 2026-09-11, Tesla officially placed the Model Y Performance on sale in China through its Chinese configurator. The Shanghai-built electric SUV is priced at 369,000 yuan, offers 460 hp and a 659 km CLTC range, and deliveries are estimated in two to six weeks. The launch restores the Performance variant to China's Model Y lineup after an absence of more than a year and a half.

events.title: Einride plans 500 Tesla electric trucks across North America
events.summary: On 2026-08-18, Sweden-based Einride AB said it plans to deploy 500 Tesla electric trucks across its North American operations. The phased rollout will begin in September 2026 and run through 2028, supporting customers including Amazon across corridors in California, Texas, New Jersey, Illinois and Georgia. Einride said the deployment would triple its electric truck fleet and be financed through th

events.title: NHTSA opens safety investigation into Tesla Cybercab
events.summary: On 2026-09-04, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an investigation into Tesla's Cybercab in the United States. The probe examines Tesla's technical data and certification of the autonomous taxi against federal safety standards, including the vehicle's lack of conventional steering and pedal controls. No operational restriction was reported.

events.title: Uber cuts more than 150 jobs at Krakow service center
events.summary: On 2026-09-06, Uber reportedly eliminated more than 150 jobs at its Krakow Business Services Center. Employees said they were expected to train workers from India to take over their duties. The cuts were described as part of global workforce reductions affecting about 3,300 people.

events.title: Tesla releases FSD safety data ahead of EU approval vote
events.summary: On 2026-09-01, Tesla publicly released safety-dashboard data for its Full Self-Driving system ahead of an expected European Union vote in October. The data supports Tesla's request for exemptions under EU rules; FSD is currently approved in five EU countries and reportedly used by more than 70,000 customers.

events.title: Tesla withdraws 20,000 vehicles over dangerous defect
events.summary: On 2026-08-19, Tesla reportedly withdrew more than 20,000 vehicles from sale because of a dangerous defect. The title does not identify the affected model, location, regulator, or specific corrective action.

events.title: NHTSA audits Tesla Cybercabs over safety certification
events.summary: On 2026-09-11, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an audit of about 1,000 Tesla Cybercab vehicles. The review examines how Tesla determined that the vehicles, which operate without steering wheels, pedals, or conventional mirrors, comply with federal safety rules. The action is a regulatory milestone for autonomous-vehicle deployment.

events.title: EVgo opens Los Angeles charging station with 20 cables
events.summary: On 2026-09-10, EVgo opened a new electric-vehicle charging station in Los Angeles, described as the city's largest non-Tesla site. The station has 20 cables, including two CHAdeMO ports capable of up to 100 kW and CCS stalls up to 350 kW. The opening expands local charging capacity and supports older EV models.

events.title: France authorizes Tesla autonomous-driving road trials
events.summary: On 2026-09-02, France authorized Tesla to test autonomous vehicles on French roads, reportedly beginning with two vehicles. Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot announced the change after speaking with Tesla president Elon Musk, reversing a July safety-based refusal. The event is a limited regulatory and autonomous-driving capability milestone, not a confirmed nationwide deployment.

events.title: NHTSA opens Tesla Cybercab safety certification probe
events.summary: On 2026-09-04, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an investigation into Tesla's certification of 1,000 Cybercab autonomous vehicles in Austin, Texas. The probe examines whether Tesla's technical data supports compliance with federal safety standards, including rules concerning vehicles without conventional manual controls. No suspension of the deployment was reported.

events.title: United States investigates Tesla Cybercab safety
events.summary: On 2026-09-07, the United States reportedly opened a safety investigation into Tesla's Cybercab. The title highlights the vehicle's lack of a steering wheel and brake pedals; no specific investigating agency or additional action is identified.

events.title: France authorizes Tesla Full Self-Driving road tests
events.summary: On 2026-09-02, France authorized and began testing two Tesla vehicles equipped with Full Self-Driving on public roads. The testing follows earlier French safety reservations and will inform a possible European-level approval decision. The system remains supervised driving, with the driver required to monitor the road and intervene.

events.title: SpaceX sues Texas officials over Terafab records
events.summary: On 2026-09-09, SpaceX reportedly filed suit in Travis County District Court against Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton and Grimes County. The company seeks to block release of records related to its proposed Terafab semiconductor and AI-hardware plant, arguing that they contain trade secrets and critical-infrastructure information.

events.title: Tesla raises Cybertruck prices by $5,000 in the United States
events.summary: On 2026-09-02, Tesla raised the starting prices of its Dual Motor AWD and Premium AWD Cybertruck models by $5,000 in the United States. The article presents the move as a pricing action intended to balance demand and profitability, while noting uncertainty about its effect on Tesla's margins and sales.

events.title: Tesla Robotaxi pushes through bollards during Austin driverless test
events.summary: On 2026-08-19, a Tesla Robotaxi operating unsupervised with passengers in Austin, Texas, drove through flexible roadside bollards after hesitating near a marked curb extension. No one was hurt and reported damage was limited to scuffed plastic, but the incident raised questions about the safety of Tesla's autonomous deployment claims.

events.title: United States urges G20 to avoid new AI regulations
events.summary: On 2026-09-01, the United States urged G20 member countries at a meeting in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, to avoid creating new institutions or rules for governing artificial intelligence. US technology adviser Michael Kratsios also advocated adoption of the Carolina Principles, which reserve new regulation for novel considerations. The proposal is part of discussions leading to the G20 leaders' su

events.title: Critics accuse Elon Musk over voter registration website
events.summary: On 2026-09-11, critics reportedly accused Elon Musk of financing Vote Safe, a voter-registration website owned by America PAC. The article says the site was allegedly designed to collect and sell users’ data to third parties, ahead of U.S. midterm elections.

events.title: Tesla unveils Cybercab autonomous taxi
events.summary: On 2026-09-05, Tesla reportedly unveiled its Cybercab autonomous taxi, according to the article title. The available evidence does not establish operational deployment, autonomous service, or a measurable capability benchmark, so the event is coded with low confidence.

events.title: Marin County investigators probe fire at Tesla dealership
events.summary: On 2026-09-07, a fire damaged four Tesla vehicles in the rear parking lot of a dealership in Corte Madera, California. Marin County fire investigators said the blaze appeared suspicious and did not appear accidental, but no motive or arrests were reported. No injuries occurred, and investigators said the fire was contained before reaching the main battery.

events.title: Tim Gruenke declines election bribery charges against Elon Musk
events.summary: On 2026-08-25, La Crosse County District Attorney Tim Gruenke, serving as special prosecutor in Madison, said Elon Musk would not face Wisconsin election-bribery charges over a proposed $1 million voter giveaway. The prosecutor said no jury would find the promise constituted bribery, noting Musk corrected the post and never paid voters.

events.title: Australian man sentenced for remotely harassing ex-partner
events.summary: On 2026-09-09, Australian justice authorities sentenced an Australian man to two years and three months in prison in Sydney after he pleaded guilty to 30 domestic-violence-related offenses involving remote control of his former partner's Tesla. The conduct reportedly included using the vehicle's systems to harass and intimidate her.

events.summary: On 2026-09-08, Qualcomm and Amazon Web Services signed a multigenerational agreement to co-develop custom AI inference chips and optical connectivity hardware. The arrangement includes a warrant for up to 25 million Qualcomm shares, vesting based on as much as $60 billion in AWS spending through 2036. Qualcomm said revenue will begin in its fiscal first quarter of 2027, with chips already in produ

events.title: Nvidia invests $3.5 billion in MediaTek convertible bonds
events.summary: On 2026-09-10, Nvidia reportedly agreed to purchase $3.5 billion of convertible bonds issued by MediaTek. In connection with the investment, MediaTek will adopt Nvidia’s NVLink Fusion technology so customers can connect custom AI accelerators to Nvidia infrastructure. The deal strengthens Nvidia’s AI platform position while giving MediaTek capital and access to Nvidia’s ecosystem.

events.title: AMD completes $4.75 billion record bond sale
events.summary: On 2026-08-15, AMD raised $4.75 billion through its largest-ever US dollar bond offering. The notes were issued in four tranches with maturities ranging from three to ten years, following AMD's commitment of up to $5 billion to Anthropic and a chip deployment partnership.

events.title: Microsoft launches Project Zenith Windows experience for AI developers
events.summary: On 2026-09-08, Microsoft presented Project Zenith at IFA Berlin as a preconfigured Windows 11 experience for developers. The image is designed for certified AMD-based devices with at least 64 GB of unified memory and supports local execution of large AI models. According to the article, Microsoft also includes Execution Containers for agentic security.

events.title: ASUS expands AI infrastructure ecosystem through strategic partnerships
events.summary: On 2026-09-03, ASUS announced an expanded AI infrastructure ecosystem at ASUS AI Tech 2026 in Seoul. The initiative spans cloud-to-edge computing and includes strategic collaborations with Intel, AMD, and other technology partners, alongside server and edge-AI platforms. The announcement describes a commercial technology milestone, but provides no investment amount or realized production scale.

events.title: AMD wins $450 million contract for Europe’s LUMI-AI supercomputer
events.summary: On 2026-09-01, EuroHPC JU and the LUMI AI Factory consortium awarded AMD a contract worth approximately $450 million for Europe's LUMI-AI supercomputer. The system will use AMD Instinct MI430X GPUs and EPYC CPUs in Bull's platform, with Nokia networking and IBM storage. The project is intended to expand Europe's sovereign AI capacity.

events.title: AMD unveils personal supercomputer for computing
events.summary: On 2026-09-08, AMD unveiled its Threadripper Halo Station workstation at a technology event in Berlin. AMD executive Jack Huynh described it as capable of running AI models with more than one trillion parameters. The product is planned for launch early next year and is expected to cost more than 100,000 euros, targeting corporate and institutional buyers.

events.title: Humain, AMD and Cisco activate Saudi AI computing platform
events.summary: On 2026-08-31, Humain, AMD and Cisco reported that an AI computing platform was up and running in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The production system uses AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs, AMD EPYC CPUs and Cisco networking to provide GPU-as-a-service for training and inference. The deployment supports Saudi Arabia's effort to build sovereign AI infrastructure.

events.title: Bull wins contract for Europe's LUMI-AI supercomputer
events.summary: On 2026-08-31, Bull was reported as the builder of the €387.8 million LUMI-AI supercomputer for EuroHPC. The system will be installed at CSC - IT Center for Science in Kajaani, Finland, and is expected to become operational in 2027. The project is a significant European sovereign AI-compute infrastructure milestone, though capacity has not yet come online.

events.title: India launches Semicon 2.0 to expand semiconductor capabilities
events.summary: On 2026-08-31, the Government of India launched Semicon 2.0 in New Delhi. Electronics and IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the programme targets development of another 100,000 semiconductor engineers and an end-to-end ecosystem spanning manufacturing, design, equipment, materials, packaging and research. India had previously developed 85,000 engineers and expanded design programmes to 355 univers

events.title: Huawei bids to build AI data centres for Egypt
events.summary: On 2026-08-26, Huawei Technologies bid to build AI data centres for the Egyptian government in Cairo. The proposal includes 2,008 Ascend chips and a 12-month construction schedule. The US State Department is reportedly seeking a rival consortium involving Nvidia, AMD and Microsoft.

events.title: HostColor expands AMD server delivery to Amsterdam, Frankfurt and Singapore
events.summary: On 2026-08-21, HostColor.com announced additional delivery locations for AMD Ryzen- and AMD EPYC-powered dedicated servers in Amsterdam, Frankfurt and Singapore. The company also increased its AMD EPYC model offerings and cited bandwidth quotas of up to 100 Gbps.

events.title: Whale Rock cuts most of its Nvidia stake in Q2
events.summary: On 2026-08-23, Whale Rock Capital Management's latest 13F filing showed it reduced its Nvidia holding by about 64%, from approximately 1.04 million shares to 377,204 shares. The filing also showed an increase in Advanced Micro Devices holdings, indicating a portfolio reallocation rather than a complete exit from AI semiconductors.

events.title: AMD releases ROCm 10 with autonomous AI optimization tools
events.summary: On 2026-08-31, AMD released ROCm 10 and made ROCm.AI generally available. The platform includes Hyperloom, described as an autonomous agentic system that profiles, optimizes and validates AI inference workloads across host code and GPU kernels. AMD reported average improvements of 3.3x for inference and 2.4x for training over ROCm 7 on the same hardware.

events.title: Geekom removes malware-laced drivers from AMD mini PCs
events.summary: On 2026-08-17, Geekom acknowledged that a legacy support page hosted a network-driver installer containing the Asruex backdoor. The company removed the package and issued guidance to affected AMD mini PC users. The incident represents a bounded software supply-chain security failure, with no reported infection scale or critical-infrastructure impact.

events.title: SIA appoints Michael Robbins as new president and CEO
events.summary: On 2026-08-19, the Semiconductor Industry Association appointed Michael Robbins as its president and CEO, effective October 1. Robbins will succeed John Neuffer, who announced his departure in January and will remain through September to support the transition. The article presents the change as a leadership succession for the U.S. semiconductor industry's policy association.

events.title: Lutnick says China declined Trump’s advanced chip offer
events.summary: On 2026-09-03, US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said at a joint press conference in Chapel Hill that China had not accepted President Donald Trump’s offer to sell advanced US AI chips. Lutnick said the lack of Chinese uptake meant further relaxation of technology export controls was unnecessary.

events.summary: On 2026-09-10, Ford Motor announced a $1 billion investment in a new paint shop at its Kentucky truck plant in Louisville. The facility is intended to replace the existing paint shop and modernize a major Ford manufacturing operation, with groundbreaking expected later this year. The announcement followed criticism from Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy regarding Ford's ties to Chinese companies

events.title: Sean Duffy demands Ford cut Chinese company ties
events.summary: On 2026-09-08, U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy sent Ford CEO Jim Farley a letter demanding changes to Ford's relationships with Chinese companies. Duffy cited national-security concerns over Chinese battery technology at a Ford plant in Michigan and Ford's continued production in China. Ford rejected the criticism and defended its U.S. battery investments.

events.title: Ford rejects Duffy request to end Chinese technology partnerships
events.summary: On 2026-09-10, Ford rejected Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy's request to end cooperation with Chinese battery and vehicle companies including CATL, Geely and BYD. Ford defended its Michigan battery investment, while the Trump administration cited national-security concerns and sought a more autonomous U.S. supply chain.

events.title: Sean Duffy urges Ford to sever ties with Chinese auto firms
events.summary: On 2026-09-10, U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy urged Ford CEO Jim Farley to sever all relationships with Chinese automotive companies. Duffy cited national-security concerns and specifically mentioned CATL, Geely and BYD. The demand was reported as being made in a letter to Ford, with no binding government order described.

events.title: Ford commits $1 billion to Louisville truck plant upgrade
events.summary: On 2026-09-12, Ford announced a $1 billion investment at its Kentucky Truck Plant in Louisville, Kentucky. The project will build a new paint shop to replace the existing facility and improve manufacturing quality and efficiency. Ford CEO Jim Farley said the investment supports American manufacturing and the Kentucky workforce.

events.title: Ford partners with Geely to co-produce cars in Europe
events.summary: On 2026-09-10, Ford reportedly reached an agreement with China's Geely to co-produce vehicles in Europe. Ford cited access to Chinese technology as necessary for global competitiveness; the article does not specify production volumes, facilities, or investment size. The partnership contrasts with Ford's support for restricting Chinese automakers in the United States.

events.title: Automotive Innovation Alliance demands Congress ban Chinese cars
events.summary: On 2026-09-08, the Alliance for Automotive Innovation sent congressional leaders a letter demanding legislation to ban the sale, import and production of Chinese vehicles and parts in the United States. The article says existing tariffs and Commerce Department regulations are viewed as temporary, prompting the request for a permanent legislative ban.

events.title: Uber launches London robotaxis using Wayve autonomous technology
events.summary: On 2026-09-03, Uber launched the UK's first commercial robotaxi service in London using Wayve's AI driving technology. The initial fleet consists of 15 Ford Mustang Mach-E vehicles, each supervised by a human safety driver. The deployment is a bounded autonomous-vehicle capability milestone rather than fully driverless operation.

events.title: Taiwan ministry funds lab to regulate tariff-free US cars
events.summary: On 2026-09-07, Taiwan's Ministry of Transportation and Communications reportedly committed about NT$400 million to build a laboratory for regulating tariff-free U.S.-made vehicles. Ford and Nissan are expected to be among the first companies to introduce vehicles, but the title does not establish that tariff-free imports have begun.

events.title: Sean Duffy criticizes Ford over Chinese technology ties
events.summary: On 2026-09-08, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy criticized Ford in a letter to CEO Jim Farley over its ties to CATL, Geely, and BYD. Duffy urged Ford to sever those relationships, citing concern about Chinese technology and manufacturing reliance. The reported action occurred in Washington, D.C., amid broader congressional criticism and White House praise for Ford.

events.title: NHTSA investigates Ford Edge coolant intrusion reports
events.summary: On 2026-09-11, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an investigation into a petition concerning coolant intrusion in the 2.0-liter EcoBoost engine used in a 2017 Ford Edge and other 2015-18 Edge vehicles. Ford said it would support the agency, while any recall would depend on a later defect and safety finding.

events.title: South Africa recalls 2,275 Ford Ranger double cabs
events.summary: On 2026-08-31, South Africa's National Consumer Commission issued a safety recall for 2,275 Ford Ranger double cabs sold between 22 May and 23 June 2026. Ford said a side-curtain airbag fault could cause the B-Pillar trim to detach during deployment, increasing injury risk. The affected vehicles were also exported to Namibia, Botswana, Lesotho and Eswatini, with dealership inspections and repairs

events.title: Ford proposes Almussafes labor framework through 2030
events.summary: On 2026-09-10, Ford presented its final proposal for a 2027–2030 labor agreement at the Almussafes plant in Spain. The offer includes annual wage increases capped at 5%, a higher annual bonus, and production flexibility measures including up to eight mandatory Saturdays per employee. The proposal is linked to potential demand growth and new-model launches planned for 2027.

events.title: Mexican Navy detains man with 84 explosives in Mazatlán
events.summary: On 2026-09-08, Mexico's Navy detained a man during a security patrol in La Noria, Mazatlán, Sinaloa. Personnel reportedly seized weapons, ammunition, ballistic equipment, vehicles, and 84 improvised explosive devices, which they inactivated before placing the suspect and seized items at the disposal of federal prosecutors.

events.title: Masked gang robs jewelry store in Sant'Angelo Lodigiano
events.summary: On 2026-08-20, a gang of at least five masked young criminals reportedly broke jewelry-store display cases with hammers at the Il Castello shopping center in Sant'Angelo Lodigiano, Italy. The suspects took valuables and fled in a Ticino-registered Ford minivan, remaining at large according to reports.

events.title: Ford appoints Shamal Al-Jazira as Iraq distributor
events.summary: On 2026-09-07, Ford reportedly appointed Shamal Al-Jazira as a new official distributor in Iraq. The title-only report provides no financial terms, exclusivity details, or broader production implications.

events.title: LG Energy Solution starts production at Lansing battery plant
events.summary: On 2026-08-18, LG Energy Solution began production at its new 226-acre battery facility in Lansing, Michigan. The plant makes LFP cells for energy-storage systems and batteries for electric vehicles, with planned annual capacity exceeding 35 GWh at full scale. LG Energy Solution Vertech will integrate the cells into utility, grid-scale, and commercial energy-storage systems.

events.title: Canadian government announces retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods
events.summary: On 2026-08-25, the Canadian government announced retaliatory tariffs of 15% to 50% on selected U.S. goods, including steel, aluminum, appliances, dairy products and electrical equipment. The measures are scheduled to take effect on September 8 after bilateral trade talks failed, escalating the Canada–United States tariff dispute.

events.title: General Motors commits over C$1 billion to Canadian plants
events.summary: On 2026-09-07, General Motors reportedly committed more than C$1 billion to its Canadian plants under a newly ratified three-year labor agreement. The investment includes returning Heavy-Duty Sierra production to Oshawa, adding North American capacity and supporting a more flexible manufacturing footprint. Workers ratified the agreement by margins of 80.5% and 96.5%.

events.title: Ultium Cells plans to restart Ohio battery plant production
events.summary: On 2026-08-14, Ultium Cells confirmed plans to restart production at its Warren, Ohio battery plant after a seven-month shutdown. The facility, a joint venture between South Korea's LG Energy Solution and General Motors, has 35 gigawatt-hours of annual battery-cell capacity. The reported decision follows GM's overhaul of its North American electrified-vehicle strategy amid weaker US BEV sales.

events.title: GM renews 20-year China joint venture with SAIC Motor
events.summary: On 2026-08-15, General Motors and SAIC Motor renewed their 50-50 joint venture in China for another 20 years. The agreement follows GM's restructuring of its Chinese operations and will support Buick exports, new-model development and access to international markets.

events.title: GM Canada ratifies contract with Unifor and commits over C$1 billion
events.summary: On 2026-09-01, GM Canada and Unifor ratified a three-year agreement covering about 4,600 workers. The agreement includes more than C$1 billion in investment in Canadian facilities, including transmission production at St. Catharines and heavy-duty pickup assembly in Oshawa. The contract also addresses wages, benefits, and job security amid pressure on Canada's auto industry.

events.title: IBM completes acquisition of HRL Laboratories
events.summary: On 2026-08-27, IBM completed its acquisition of HRL Laboratories, which was jointly owned by Boeing and General Motors. Financial terms were not disclosed. HRL brings silicon-spin qubit research and longstanding defense, aerospace and automotive technology programs, while IBM said its partnerships with Boeing and General Motors will continue.

events.title: General Motors plans C$1.1 billion Canadian production investment
events.summary: On 2026-08-30, General Motors reported plans to invest C$1.1 billion in its Canadian operations under a tentative agreement with Unifor. The package includes C$144 million for GM’s Oshawa assembly plant to prepare for next-generation heavy-duty GMC Sierra production, alongside previously announced Ontario engine investment. The plans come as Canadian vehicles face U.S. tariff pressure.

events.title: Automotive Innovation Alliance demands Congress ban Chinese cars
events.summary: On 2026-09-08, the Alliance for Automotive Innovation sent congressional leaders a letter demanding legislation to ban the sale, import and production of Chinese vehicles and parts in the United States. events.title: Plasman invests $10 million in Windsor molding technology
events.summary: On 2026-09-09, Plasman unveiled four injection molding machines at its Windsor 1 Manufacturing facility in Oldcastle, Ontario. The company invested $10 million to expand production, improve energy efficiency and bring work in-house for new Honda and General Motors programs, securing 18 additional jobs.

events.title: NHTSA expands investigation into General Motors V8 engine failures
events.summary: On 2026-08-22, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration's Office of Defects Investigation opened an engineering analysis of General Motors' 6.2-liter V8 engine failures. The review follows a 2025 recall covering 597,630 trucks and SUVs and complaints that engines failed after repairs or replacements. The article does not report a final enforcement decision.

events.title: General Motors orders service fix for loose oil filters
events.summary: On 2026-09-10, General Motors reportedly issued Service Update N262568830 to dealers concerning under-torqued oil filters in select 2026 and 2027 Chevrolet, GMC, and Cadillac vehicles. Dealers are instructed to torque the filters, clean residual oil, and top off engine oil at no charge to owners.

events.title: General Motors keeps idled CAMI plant open for defence opportunities
events.summary: On 2026-08-29, General Motors committed not to sell or close its idled CAMI assembly plant in Ingersoll, Ontario. According to Unifor's bargaining report, GM will give the facility first consideration for Canadian Armed Forces work if the automaker receives a government contract. The commitment preserves potential future investment but does not announce a production restart.

events.title: Mark Carney urges opposition leaders to unite on trade
events.summary: On 2026-08-25, Prime Minister Mark Carney spoke by phone with Canadian opposition party leaders in Ottawa about trade negotiations with the United States. Carney briefed them on Canada’s new response measures and urged a united “Team Canada” approach to protect jobs and Canadian interests.

The filing said the alleged scheme operated across several markets, including China, with approximately $350 million retained in a rebate pool in 2024.

events.title: Rivian CFO Claire McDonough to leave and join GE Vernova
events.summary: On 2026-08-27, Rivian Automotive announced that CFO Claire McDonough will resign effective October 30. McDonough is pursuing a new opportunity and will join GE Vernova, while Rivian said the departure is not due to disagreement with management or its board. The change comes as Rivian expands production and sales of its R2 electric SUV.
